$comment: The single source of the product-volume formatting rule (ADR-0056, decision 4). PHP, TypeScript and Dart each implement the rule and each language's test suite reads THIS FILE. A new vector belongs here, never in one suite. The unit is preceded by a no-break space (U+00A0) so a size never wraps across a line.

rule.below_threshold: Whole millilitres: '<n> ml'. Below 100 ml the litre value has no non-zero first decimal, and below 5 ml it rounds to zero outright.
rule.at_or_above_threshold: Litres, at most two decimals, trailing zeros dropped.
rule.rounding: Half away from zero at hundredths of a litre, computed on integers: hundredths = (ml + 5) div 10. No float decides a boundary.
rule.decimal_separator: The reader's: ',' for de, '.' for en.
rule.unknown_language: Falls back to the decimal comma, in all three implementations. A size in the wrong punctuation is a smaller failure than a statement or a card that does not render at all.
rule.grouping: None. The validated maximum is 10 000 ml = 10 l, so no value ever groups.
rule.null: A product with no volume formats to nothing at all; the caller prints the name alone.
